manual_review.rule: Each hit or exposure is a lead for a manual reading (controlled.audit_fresh_attempt_transcript). Every flagged access was read in its transcript. An attempt that read anything outside its workspace fails and is excluded; an attempt that only read or listed its own workspace, or touched only system locations, passes.
manual_review.note: 'excluded' above is the script's own list of flagged attempts. After the reading, the attempts excluded from every analysis are those in excluded_after_review; each candidate's attempt record carries the verdict (audit.passed).
manual_review.independent_sweep: Beyond the flagged accesses, every tool call of the 20 transcripts was read for this review: the paths of the file tools, each shell command's working directory and the absolute and relative paths it names, the host programs it ran, and every tool other than the file tools, the shell and the final hand-back. No file tool named a path outside its workspace, and no Grep or Glob ran without a path. Every shell command but two began with a cd into the workspace; those two printed the instruction file by its absolute workspace path. Every relative parent reference resolved inside the workspace. Besides the shell's standard utilities and git, the host programs run were the system python3 and, in one attempt, ruff, all on workspace files only. One attempt (CS-04-fresh-B-final-1) called a session-archiving tool once, which was denied and returned nothing. The wrappers and instruction file of every workspace are unchanged.
manual_review.outside_scope: Harness context that is not a tool input or output was not scanned by the script: every attempt was given the build session's environment details (its working directory and scratch path), and 16 of the 20 received reminders listing the build session's task titles and descriptions. Read for this review, they hold no reference, transcript, verifier, candidate or label of CS-04; no attempt used a task tool or opened a path they name.
